divergence_finding.headline: THE REAL WASTE IS A DIVERGENCE REGIME, NOT SEED NOISE. This supersedes and corrects the previous cycle's noise_floor_finding, which misdiagnosed the problem. ~52% of full-rung compute produced garbage, and it is almost perfectly predicted by lr.
divergence_finding.method: All 379 full-rung (epochs=27) arms split on BPC < 3.0 (converged, n=181, median 2.3057) vs >= 3.0 (diverged, n=198). Then divergence rate cross-tabulated by lr band.
divergence_finding.reconfirmed_this_cycle: Repull of all 519 runs reproduces the monotone collapse (0.79 -> 0.00). Band edges differ slightly from last cycle's table (this cycle bins at 0.0009/0.0011/0.0012/0.0013/0.0014), so the per-band counts are not identical, but the shape and the 0.00 at lr>=0.0014 are unchanged.
divergence_finding.consequence_1_the_old_noise_floor_was_an: The previous cycle reported sigma=0.0299 BPC by pooling arms across ALL lr including the divergent ones. That number is not run-to-run noise - it is the tail of a bimodal distribution. Restricting to the converged regime (lr>=0.0012) and excluding diverged arms, the median within-config robust sigma is 0.0128 BPC (last cycle) / 0.0102 BPC (this cycle's estimator, 4 replicated groups, MAD*1.4826). So the sweep is ~2.3-3x LESS noisy than believed.
divergence_finding.consequence_2_but_noise_is_still_not_the: At sigma ~0.0102-0.0128, the top-12 full-rung spread is 0.0120 BPC = ~1 sigma, and 18/97 converged high-lr arms sit within 1 sigma of the record. Ranks 1-12 remain a coin flip. Replication is still required - but it is required to rank, not to avoid garbage.
divergence_finding.consequence_3_the_fix_is_narrow_lr_not_n: Because divergence is monotone in lr and reaches 0.0 at lr>=0.0014, the single highest-value search-space change is to move the lr range UP and make it discrete, so the search stops spending half the budget on arms that cannot converge.
divergence_finding.consequence_4_hyperband_eta3_cannot_save: Client-side Hyperband prunes on val/ce_final, so a diverged arm IS pruned early - which is why the wasted GPU-time is only ~13% even though 52% of arms are garbage. The waste is in run COUNT and in the run_cap budget, not in wall-clock. run_cap 96 with a safe lr range is therefore close to compute-neutral.

depth_x_lr_interaction.headline: NEW THIS CYCLE, AND IT IS THE JUSTIFICATION FOR THIS CYCLE'S ONLY DESIGN CHANGE: the optimal lr is DEPTH-DEPENDENT, and both 0-run candidate sweeps had it wrong for their own pinned depth.
depth_x_lr_interaction.method: Full-rung converged arms, each arm scored as the delta between its BPC and the median of its OWN chunk_dec_layers cell (so depth is differenced out and lr is left as the only moving part inside a depth cell - verified: within the chunk_dec_layers=10 core cell only lr varies). Two cohorts: SHALLOW chunk_dec_layers<=8, DEEP chunk_dec_layers>=10. Only lr levels with n>=2 reported.
depth_x_lr_interaction.reading: DEEP models want lr ~0.00137-0.00139 (best deltas anywhere in the project: -0.0242 at 0.00138, -0.0211 at 0.00139, and the two best single arms in history, 6l5qdkou 2.2411 @ lr 0.00138 and s9gnov0d 2.2418 @ 0.00139). SHALLOW models are best at ~0.00135 (-0.0596) and the 0.0014 cell is the worst point in the shallow table (+0.1911, n=2, ~15 sigma). Absolute ladders tell the same story: at chunk_dec_layers=4, lr 0.00145 gives 2.3635 and 0.00147 gives 2.3659 (n=3) against 2.2894 at 0.00136; at chunk_dec_layers=6, lr 0.00136-0.00141 gives 2.4276 / 2.4222 - the only arms in the whole high-lr region that are clearly degraded-but-not-diverged.
depth_x_lr_interaction.why_it_matters_here: BOTH candidate sweeps pin chunk_dec_layers=8, i.e. the shallow cohort. 08wxlqx1 (the currently-pointed-to sweep) puts its ENTIRE lr axis at {0.0014, 0.00145} - the two levels at which shallow models are worst. Its historical evidence at cdl=8 stops at lr 0.0013 (2.2714, n=2); there is not one cdl=8 arm above 0.0013 anywhere in the project's history. m3gdk0yc's lr {0.00136, 0.00139} is inside the measured-stable band and is adopted here.
depth_x_lr_interaction.caveats: n per lr cell is 2-4, so single cells are noisy; the SHALLOW 0.00143-0.00148 entries (-0.067 to -0.079) contradict a simple 'high lr is bad when shallow' story and are probably confounded by co-varying knobs. The claim this cycle actually relies on is the narrow, safe one: 0.00136 and 0.00139 sit inside the band where every cohort is at or below its own-depth median, while 0.0014 and 0.00145 do not.

ffn_inference_finding.headline: NEW: chunk_dec_dim_ff=null is INSIDE the 2048 cap, inferred from params/count. This closes an open question that four previous cycles flagged as unverifiable, and it is what makes xppnwnpn provably cap-clean rather than cap-clean-by-assumption.
ffn_inference_finding.why_it_was_open: The GPU sweep kernel's train_src.py is NOT in this repository (kernels/perpos-gpu-sweep/_private_live/ contains only sweep_config.json), so there is no source to read and no coerce_config to inspect. All 467 historical arms logged chunk_dec_dim_ff=null, so the resolved value has never been observable from config echoes.
ffn_inference_finding.method: params/count is a clean function of chunk_dec_layers at fixed (d_model, quantized_dim, token_dec_dim_ff, ch). Fit per-layer slope from consecutive depth levels and solve for the chunk-decoder width W and FF under a standard layer's param count a*W^2 + 2*W*FF with FF = k*W.

evidence.d_model_1024: slope 1.580-1.612M params per chunk_dec_layer, identical across q=128/q=256 and tokFF 512/1024
evidence.d_model_512_and_768: slope 0.397M per layer (both identical, so both resolve to the same W)
evidence.implied: W = d_model/2, i.e. W=512 at d_model=1024, and 4*W^2 + 2*W*W = 6*W^2 matches the measured slope, so FF ~= W
evidence.conclusion: chunk_dec_dim_ff=null resolves to approximately 512 when d_model=1024 - 4x inside the 2048 cap. It is NOT 4096 and NOT 2048.

ffn_inference_finding.second_thing_it_settles: The per-layer slope is IDENTICAL for quantized_dim=128 and 256 (1.580M both). So quantized_dim does not change model capacity at all in this codebase - it only changes the compression bottleneck. That is consistent with, and independently explains, the inertness measured in axis_effects_finding.
ffn_inference_finding.residual_risk: This is inference from an integer param count across 5 depth levels at 2 scales, not source inspection. It is solid enough to trust for cap-compliance (512 vs a 2048 cap is a 4x margin that no plausible rounding flips) but it should be confirmed by reading the kernel source if that source is ever added to the repo.
ffn_inference_finding.consequence_for_folding: xppnwnpn is cap-clean on all four caps by construction AND by inference: token_dec_dim_ff in {128,256} (cap 256), token_dec_layers=1 (cap 2), chunk_dec_layers=8 (cap 8, exactly at cap), chunk_dec_dim_ff=null -> ~512 (cap 2048). If it runs, its arms are the first genuinely foldable GPU data this project will have.

aliasing_finding.headline: NEW AND IMPORTANT: in all 467 historical arms, every auxiliary knob is 100% ALIASED with chunk_dec_layers. Each depth cell contains exactly one value of clip_grad, token_lr_mult, comp_lr_mult, token_wd, lambda_snap, prior_aux_weight, refiner_target_scale, compressor_emb_dim, learned_pos and clw. Zero degrees of freedom - no auxiliary effect in this project is identified.
aliasing_finding.method: Stratify the converged high-lr arms by chunk_dec_layers and tabulate the distinct values of each candidate knob inside each depth cell. A knob with >1 distinct value inside a depth cell would be identified; none has one.
aliasing_finding.evidence: At chunk_dec_layers=10 every one of the 21 arms has clip_grad=1.0, token_lr_mult=0.5, comp_lr_mult=1.5, token_wd=0.01, lambda_snap=0.02, prior_aux_weight=0.5, refiner_target_scale=0.5, weight_decay=0.01, warmup_steps=512. Same story at 12 (n=16) and 14 (n=22).
aliasing_finding.what_it_invalidates: (1) The 2026-09-28 cycle's 'token_dec_dropout is worth 0.025 BPC (0.8 sigma)' - within any depth cell token_dec_dropout takes exactly one value, so that delta was depth, not dropout. (2) The loose-control aux ladders that at first glance show clip_grad 0.5->1.0 worth -0.059, token_lr_mult 0.5->0.7 worth +0.042 and comp_lr_mult 1.5->2.0 worth +0.051 - ALL of those are pure depth confound, because the 'good' aux values happen to sit in the deep cells. (3) Any statement that the record arm's auxiliary settings (clip 0.5, token_lr_mult 0.7, comp_lr_mult 2, token_wd 0.02, lambda_snap 0.05, prior_aux_weight 0.25, refiner_target_scale 0.7, learned_pos True) are good - they were never compared against anything at the same depth.
aliasing_finding.what_survives: Only effects identified WITHIN a depth cell: lr (the sole free axis inside each cell, which is why depth_x_lr_interaction is trustworthy), depth itself, and the axes that the two 08wxlqx1 / m3gdk0yc designs finally vary at fixed depth - clw, cdd and tokFF.
aliasing_finding.consequence_for_xppnwnpn: Its aux pins are inherited from the record arm and are therefore NOT validated at chunk_dec_layers=8. That is a known, accepted risk: the first 96 arms will measure clw x cdd x tokFF at a fixed set of unvalidated aux pins. If a run at cdl=8 lands far above the 2.27 that cdl=8 achieved historically, the aux pins - not clw - are the first suspect, and the follow-up sweep should spend its budget there.
aliasing_finding.correction_2026_10_04: SUPERSEDED IN ITS MECHANISM - see aliasing_finding_correction. The aux knobs are not 100% aliased: they take 2-3 values inside chunk_dec_layers=4. The cell is an unreplicated random search, so the conclusion (no aux effect identified) stands but for a different reason.

clw_redundancy_finding.headline: NEW: chunk_local_window is measured in TOKEN positions, so at the GPU sweep's block_size=256 the level 256 is IDENTICAL to None. Sweep m3gdk0yc (PR #207) spent 25% of its 96-arm design on that duplicate.
clw_redundancy_finding.evidence_for_token_units: chunk_local_window=16 at block_size=256, ch=4 is 16 tokens = exactly 4 characters = 1 chunk - the prior cycle already identified it as 'a near-degenerate 1-chunk window', which only makes sense in token units. It is also consistent with the TPU side, where the best run uses clw=256 at block_size=512, i.e. half-context in tokens.
clw_redundancy_finding.consequence: At block_size=256 a window of 256 tokens admits every position, so {None, 64, 128, 256} collapses to three distinct operating points (full attention at n=6 across two cells, plus 64 and 128 at n=3 each). xppnwnpn keeps {None, 32, 64, 128} - four distinct levels, including the half-context point 128 that the TPU evidence actually points at.
clw_redundancy_finding.robustness: The conclusion does not depend on the unit question. If clw were in CHUNK positions instead, the full context at block_size=256, ch=4 is 64 chunks, and a level of 256 would still be clamped to full attention - i.e. still a duplicate of None. Under both readings, 256 is redundant at this block size.

axis_effects_finding.headline: Stratified effect sizes (each axis compared inside (chunk_dec_layers, token_dec_dim_ff) cells, converged high-lr arms only), so these are the effects that survive the aliasing in aliasing_finding.
axis_effects_finding.d_model: +0.29 BPC for 768 vs 1024, consistent across all 3 cells (+0.3194/+0.2283/+0.2909). Second-largest real effect in the data; d_model=1024 is correctly pinned.
axis_effects_finding.chunk_dec_layers: monotone, -0.02 to -0.03 BPC from 8 to 14. Real but bought with 1.7x params and 1.36x wall-clock, i.e. forbidden compute inflation. Cap stays.
axis_effects_finding.quantized_dim: INERT. 128 vs 256 median penalty +0.0002 BPC across 4 stratified cells (min 0.0000, max 0.1057 in one n=2-vs-n=4 cell). q has no capacity effect at all - see ffn_inference_finding, the per-layer param slope is identical at q=128 and q=256. So xppnwnpn's q=256 pin is harmless, and the open question of matching the TPU best run's q=128 is not worth GPU time.
axis_effects_finding.chunk_dec_dropout: 0.1 beats 0 by a median +0.0340 BPC across 4 cells (+0.0098 to +0.1508). TPU's best run uses 0.2; xppnwnpn keeps {0.1, 0.2} as a real 2-level axis.
axis_effects_finding.chunk_local_window (16 vs None, all the: +0.0149 median penalty for 16, with the SIGN FLIPPING across cells (16 is better in 2 of 4 cells, worse in 2). This is far weaker than the TPU-side 0.45 BPC monotone story and it is the single biggest reason to run the 4-level GPU axis rather than keep importing the TPU conclusion.
axis_effects_finding.token_dec_dropout / compressor_emb_dim /: 0 vs 0.1 inert; comp_emb 64 beats 32 by ~0.02; token_wd 0.02 mildly ahead of 0.01/0.05 (+0.0275 median) - and 0.02 is what xppnwnpn pins, so that pin happens to agree with the only weakly-identified evidence available.

record_is_compute_lean.headline: The record is rejected on the CAP and on the FOLD BAR, never on compute - it is CHEAPER than the median converged arm, not more expensive.
record_is_compute_lean.numbers: 65dr5rv3 (2.2378 BPC): 10.34M params, 10666s. Median converged high-lr arm: 16.72M params, 11582s. So the record is 0.62x the parameters and 0.92x the wall-clock of a typical converged arm in this project.
record_is_compute_lean.why_this_matters: The skill's rejection rule is 'a config whose only edge is more compute is not a valid improvement'. That rule does not fire here - the record's edge is not bought with compute. It is still NOT foldable, for two independent reasons: token_dec_dim_ff=512 exceeds the hard cap of 256 (and the GPU kernel does not clamp, see kernel_clamp_finding), and 2.2378 is 0.3545 BPC worse than baseline.json current_best 1.8833. Both must hold, and neither is about compute.
record_is_compute_lean.top5_all_compute_inflated: Ranks 2-5 (x7vuvvus, 6l5qdkou, s9gnov0d, 4uhzwo5y) ARE rejected as inflation: chunk_dec_layers=14 > cap 8, token_dec_dim_ff=1024 > cap 256, 23.04M params (2.23x the record) and 15.0-17.3ks (1.4-1.6x the record) for +0.0028 to +0.0050 BPC (0.22-0.39 sigma). Rank 1 is not in that class.
record_is_compute_lean.reconfirmed_2026_10_04: params/count for the record is 10336079 and for the median converged high-lr arm 16720207; the inflation rule therefore still does not fire on rank 1. Its rejection rests on the token_dec_dim_ff cap and on being n=1.

clw_finding.headline: chunk_local_window IS THE LARGEST EFFECT IN THE ENTIRE PROJECT, AND THE GPU SWEEP HAD IT PINNED AT THE WRONG END. This is the most important new finding of this cycle.
clw_finding.tpu_side_evidence: At the committed budget (10M/512/bs384), chunk_local_window is monotone and huge: None -> median 2.2969 (n=4), 64 -> 2.0511 (n=7), 128 -> 1.9770 (n=2), 256 -> 1.9604 (n=27), and the single best TPU run in the project (pvz94wfa, 1.84410 BPC) uses clw=256. That is a 0.45 BPC spread from one architecture knob - larger than every other knob measured, combined.
clw_finding.gpu_side_gap: The GPU sweep had only ever sampled chunk_local_window in {None, 16}. 16 is a near-degenerate window at block_size=256 (it is 1 chunk at ch=4), so it is not the same operating point as TPU's 256 at block_size=512. And the prior cycle's candidate 8p4t1juu had PINNED it to [null] - i.e. it pinned away the exact axis that carries the largest known effect, and pinned it at the value that is 0.45 BPC WORST on the TPU side.
clw_finding.why_the_two_operating_points_are_compara: clw is measured in token positions at a fixed block_size. TPU runs block_size=512 with clw=256 (half-context). GPU runs block_size=256. The transferable claim is not 'use 256' but 'a moderate local window beats full attention and beats a degenerate one', which is exactly the shape [null,32,64,128] tests.
clw_finding.gpu_side_weak_evidence_for_direction: REVISED THIS CYCLE, and it is much weaker than the TPU number suggests. Stratifying the converged high-lr arms by (chunk_dec_layers, token_dec_dim_ff), the only clw contrast the GPU history contains - 16 vs None - carries a median penalty of just +0.0149 BPC for 16, and the SIGN FLIPS across cells (16 wins 2 of 4, loses 2 of 4). So on the GPU side's own operating point (block_size=256, ch=4, 64 chunk positions) windowing is worth ~0.015 BPC with no consistent sign, not 0.45. The TPU-side spread conflates block_size 512 vs 256, depth, and dropout. This does NOT make the axis worthless - it makes it unmeasured where it matters, which is exactly why xppnwnpn runs it as a 4-level exhaustive axis at n=3 instead of inheriting the TPU conclusion. See clw_redundancy_finding for the level choice.
clw_finding.steering: chunk_local_window: [null, 32, 64, 128] - 4 distinct, non-redundant levels (256 would duplicate None at block_size=256), n=3 each by construction.

best.run_name: zesty-sweep-18 (sweep 2rdefl3u); still unbeaten after 7 further generations = 519 runs total, newest 2026-08-24

best.reliability_caveat: REVISED AGAIN, and this is the sharpest version yet. (a) REPLICATION: an exhaustive match on the record's non-lr config finds EXACTLY ONE arm in 519 - the record itself. Its own converged high-lr group (cdl=6 / tokFF=512) has n=2, but that second arm differs in another knob. The record is a single unreplicated draw, not a two-of-two. (b) IDENTIFICATION: see aliasing_finding_correction - the aux knobs are not literally 100% aliased, but the one cell where they vary is a 111-arm RANDOM SEARCH with one arm per config, which is also underpowered (34 converged arms, 21 regression columns, no |t|>2). (c) MAGNITUDE: the top-12 spread is 0.0120 BPC ~ 1 sigma (within-config sigma 0.0114 today), so ranks 1-12 remain a coin flip. Do not treat 2.2378 as a demonstrated lead and do not treat its config as a good default.

aliasing_finding_correction.headline: CORRECTION to the 2026-10-03 aliasing_finding: the aux knobs are NOT 100% aliased with chunk_dec_layers. They DO vary inside chunk_dec_layers=4 (2-3 distinct values each). The CONCLUSION survives - no aux effect is identified - but the stated MECHANISM was wrong, and the difference matters for what to do next.
aliasing_finding_correction.measured: Within chunk_dec_layers=4 (n=111 arms, 100 metric-bearing, 34 converged): clip_grad {0.5:37, 1:74}, token_lr_mult {0.7:48, 0.5:63}, comp_lr_mult {2:89, 1.5:22}, token_wd {0.01,0.02,0.05}, lambda_snap {0,0.02,0.05}, prior_aux_weight {0.25,0.5,0.75}, refiner_target_scale {0.35,0.5,0.7}, compressor_emb_dim {32:24, 64:87}, learned_pos {T:66, F:45}, chunk_local_window {None:49, 16:62}, weight_decay {0.001, 0.01}, warmup_steps {512, 1024}. All deeper depth cells still carry a single value, which is where the earlier claim came from.
aliasing_finding_correction.why_it_is_still unidentified: The cdl=4 cell is a RANDOM SEARCH, not a factorial: 111 arms produce 111 distinct configs once lr is excluded, and lr is unique per arm. So there is no replication anywhere in it either. Fitting main effects on the 34 converged arms (OLS: intercept + lr + lr^2 + 18 knob dummies, p=21, R2=0.657, resid_sd=0.2295) yields NO coefficient above |t|=2 - the largest is warmup_steps 1024->512 at -0.246 BPC, t=-1.93, which does not clear a Bonferroni threshold for 30 tests. Consistent with the 2026-10-03 verdict, reached by a different route.
aliasing_finding_correction.what_it_invalidates_in_the_old_note: The 2026-10-03 phrasing 'zero degrees of freedom - no auxiliary effect in this project is identified' overstated the mechanism for cdl=4, and the implication that cdl=4 data could not be used at all is wrong: it can support a (weak) main-effect fit, and that fit is what rules the aux pins in or out.
aliasing_finding_correction.what_it_implies_for_the_design: The designated sweep's aux pins are inherited from the record arm and remain unvalidated at chunk_dec_layers=8 - there is genuinely no GPU evidence for or against them at any depth. That risk is unchanged and is restated in no_successor_decision.
